lines.text: A company trusted to guard the internet picked the number four as its secret key.
When you open a website, your browser checks its ID card, called a certificate, to make sure the site is real.
lines.title: How your browser checks a website

lines.text: Those ID cards are signed by certificate authorities. Think of them as the passport office of the internet.
lines.title: Who signs the ID cards?

lines.text: Their secret signing key should be a giant number, over a hundred digits. But eMudhra used tiny numbers. One was just four.
lines.title: eMudhra's secret key

lines.text: With a key that small, anyone could work it out and forge an ID card for any website. Your bank. Your email. Anything.
lines.title: Anyone could fake an ID card

lines.text: Cloudflare patched within hours. It spotted about one hundred sixty forged certificates, but no sign of spying.
lines.title: Cloudflare patched within hours

lines.text: The scary part? More than half of the big networks it tested still trusted the bad keys.
lines.title: More than half still trusted the bad keys

lines.text: So keep your phone and browser updated. That is how your device learns who not to trust.
lines.title: What you can do

points.text: Updates teach your device who not to trust
